cleared.check: Task 4, Monad native code. The callTracer trees of the 16 scripts (from bor at quiknode and, separately, from rpc.monad.xyz) were converted to the input of cycle 16's replay harness (rp for v0.16.7, rp165 for v0.16.5) with the fresh address written as Monad's PoolManager address, and every PoolManager frame was run by Monad's interpreter and by native code from Monad's x86 emitter, with all other calls answered from the tree.
cleared.result: Interpreter and native code give identical digests (status, gas and output of each frame, persistent and transient storage, balance, logs) for all 16 scripts and 743 PoolManager frames on both releases, and the v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 digests are identical to each other. Every frame's status and output equal the recorded tree. Against the Monad node's own frame gas, all 389 set 1 frames are equal; 31 of 354 set 2 frames differ by exactly 10,000 or 25,000 gas, and each of those frames makes a call to a hook double, the token double or precompile 4 that the harness answers from the tree, so the difference sits in the harness's model of answered calls (it treats every account as existing).

cleared.check: Task 5. The most expensive single call of the 16 scripts is the swap of set 1 script 67 at tick spacing 1 across most of the range: 61.9M gas on Polygon, 80.1M on Monad, 39.5M on Tempo (traced frame gas). Per-transaction caps: Polygon 33,554,432 (EIP-7825 with 2^25 since Madhugiri, block 80,084,800), block limit 160M; Monad 30M per transaction, 150M per block, gas charged on the limit; Tempo 30M per transaction and 30M per block for non-payment transactions inside a 500M block; Ethereum 16,777,216 per transaction.
cleared.result: That swap fits one transaction on none of the three networks (nor on Ethereum). It is a delay without loss and is already recorded (F-039, F-063, F-064, F-111, F-115): a swapper reaches the same price in several transactions with intermediate sqrtPriceLimitX96, because the loop stops at the limit (src/libraries/Pool.sol:344, 364). Liquidity removal cannot be made to exceed a transaction: Pool.modifyLiquidity touches only the two ticks of the position, their bitmap bits and the position (src/libraries/Pool.sol:146-215), with no loop over other ticks, and the heaviest modifyLiquidity in these scripts used 208,247 gas on Polygon and 180,579 on Monad. Donate, take, burn and clear have no loop either. No pool state an ordinary account can build makes a removal or a claim withdrawal need more gas than a transaction may carry, so there is no freeze.

leads.question: Can set 2's full-range scripts be split on Tempo's official endpoint (tempo/v1.19.1) by a hook double that also forwards a mint or burn to the PoolManager under a reserved selector, so the hook-address deltas can be rebuilt between parts?
leads.why: Set 2 on Tempo is matched only through drpc's debug_traceCall, whose build is hidden; a split on the official endpoint would tie the answer to a named release before T14 on 8 December 2026.

leads.question: Why does Monad's callTracer report 10,000 gas more (or 25,000 less for a value call to precompile 4) than the replay harness for PoolManager frames that call a contract placed by state override?
leads.why: The difference is confined to calls the harness answers from the tree, but it is not explained from Monad's source, and harness gas is the evidence used for frame gas equality.

leadResults.answer: Polygon: polygon-bor-rpc.publicnode.com now grants 1e9 gas and rpc-mainnet.matic.quiknode.pro 600M; all 16 scripts finish and equal the full Ethereum answer word for word. Monad: the 150M cap is enough for all 16 on three endpoints, all equal; cycle 17's list was a comparison with a 25M Ethereum reference that had itself run out of gas. Tempo: official eth_call is capped at 50M; set 1 finishes in split form on the official v1.19.1 node and set 2 through debug_traceCall at 600M on tempo.drpc.org, all equal. The worst swap (set 1 script 67) uses 61.9M on Polygon, 80.1M on Monad and 39.5M on Tempo, above the per-transaction caps of 33.6M, 30M and 30M; this is the known delay without loss, and liquidity removal has no loop, so there is no freeze. Monad's interpreter and native code on v0.16.7 and v0.16.5 agree on all 743 frames.
Not attempted in this cycle: running set 2 with a real TIP-20 precompile as currency1 needs the token's balance layout in precompile storage, which this unit did not establish.
